en: Udāna 2.5 Upāsakasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a certain lay follower from Icchānaṅgala had arrived at Sāvatthī on some business.
Having finished that business in Sāvatthī, the lay follower approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
As that lay follower was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this to him:
“It has been a long time, lay follower, since you made the occasion to come here.

“For a long time, Bhante, I have desired to approach the Blessed One for a visit, but I have been occupied with various duties and obligations. Thus, I was unable to approach the Blessed One for a visit.”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“Truly, there is nothing whatsoever that brings suffering to him who has mastered the Dhamma and is well-versed in it.”
being tormented, a person bound among people.
